monthly_review.summary: September shows a clear shift toward higher-intensity running: volume increased sharply (+22.1 km), pace improved significantly (+35 sec/km faster), zone distribution shifted markedly toward Z3–Z4, and cadence rose while efficiency slightly declined — consistent with a deliberate build phase.
monthly_review.highlight: The 35-sec/km pace improvement alongside a +7 bpm average HR and 33% of time in Zone 3 — up from 26% last month — reflects a sustained, multi-month intensity shift confirmed by the 2026-07 to 2026-09 progression (Z3%: 29% → 29% → 33%).

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance (73.4 vs 51.3 km) and run count (14 vs 10) — no additional sessions or km are needed in the remaining 4 days. Given missing recovery data, prioritizing consistency over further volume gain is prudent.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance correlates with declining efficiency
insights.body: Zone 3 share rose from 26% (Aug) to 33% (Sep), coinciding with efficiency worsening from 14.12 to 14.6 ml/kg/km — the largest monthly increase in this metric since May (13.42). This suggests accumulated Z3 work may be outpacing neuromuscular adaptation.

insights.title: Stable aerobic decoupling despite rising intensity
insights.body: Recent runs show aerobic TE between 2.4–3.1%, all under 5% — even during faster efforts like 7.4 km at 8:08/km (2.9%) and 4.7 km at 7:26/km (3.1%). This indicates preserved aerobic integrity despite higher load.

insights.title: Cadence–stride length trade-off emerging
insights.body: Cadence dropped from 149 spm (Aug) to 145 spm (Sep) while stride length increased (e.g., 86.49 cm on 2026-09-24 vs 76.39 cm on 2026-09-13), suggesting a shift toward longer, less frequent strides — possibly linked to fatigue or pacing strategy.

insights.title: Best pace acceleration without VO₂max change
insights.body: Best 1-km pace improved from 453 sec/km (7:33) in Aug to 369 sec/km (6:09) in Sep — a dramatic 84-sec gain — yet VO₂max remains stable at 41–42 mL/kg/min, implying gains are likely neuromuscular or metabolic (e.g., lactate buffering), not central aerobic.

recommendations.action: Zone 2 run: 6 km at HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm, on Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Restores aerobic base while reinforcing efficient turnover after recent Z3-heavy load; aligns with stable HRV-inferred adequacy but avoids pushing recovery limits.

recommendations.action: Strides + form drill session: 6 × 15-sec fast-leg cycles off 5-min easy jog, focusing on quick turnover and minimal vertical oscillillation (<8.0 cm)
recommendations.reason: Addresses rising vertical oscillation (8.2–8.6 cm in last 4 runs) and cadence dip — both associated with fatigue-induced inefficiency.

recommendations.action: Complete one full rest day with ≥7.5 hours sleep and no structured activity on Thursday
recommendations.reason: Compensates for missing recovery data by proactively safeguarding against cumulative fatigue — especially given 14 runs this month and elevated Z3 exposure.

risk_flags.evidence: Running economy worsened from 14.12 to 14.6 ml/kg/km (+0.48) while Z3% increased 7 pts and aerobic TE rose 0.3 pts — a triad suggesting diminishing returns from current intensity mix.
risk_flags.action: Reduce Z3 volume by ~20% next month unless efficiency rebounds to ≤14.2 ml/kg/km.

risk_flags.evidence: Vertical oscillation increased from 7.7–7.9 cm (early Sep) to 8.3–8.6 cm (late Sep), ground contact time rose to 318 ms on 2026-09-18, and cadence fell — all biomechanical signs of reduced spring efficiency.
risk_flags.action: Insert two stride-focused sessions and monitor vertical oscillation trend weekly.

weekly_focus.theme: Consolidate intensity gains with aerobic resilience
weekly_focus.description: Balance the clear progress in speed and Z3 tolerance with deliberate reinforcement of efficiency, recovery responsiveness, and movement economy — preventing premature fatigue-driven regression.
